title: Execution Telemetry Quorum and Sampling Policy
author: Eleanor Chen
content:
Summary

This page defines the Execution Telemetry Quorum and Sampling Policy for Redwood's serving runtime. It explains the signals we collect, the quorum rules used to trigger high-fidelity capture, the sampling knobs available to runtime operators and SREs, and operational playbooks for incidents and benchmarks. The goal is to balance diagnostic fidelity for production incidents and regressions with telemetry cost and privacy constraints.

Why this matters

- Full-fidelity traces for all requests are prohibitively expensive (bandwidth, storage, ingestion cost).
- Certain failures and regressions only manifest under narrow execution cohorts; a simple uniform sampler reduces reproducibility.
- Kernel-level scheduling signals, KV-cache deltas, and cross-device handoff traces are high-value for root-cause analysis but high-cost to capture.
- We need a deterministic, auditable policy that: preserves SLO observability, limits cost, enables postmortem reproducibility, and supports controlled ramping during experiments.

Scope and definitions

- Execution telemetry: structured traces, kernel scheduling events, per-kernel latency histograms, KV cache hit/miss traces, device-to-device handoff events, and request provenance metadata.
- Quorum: a multi-signal predicate that determines whether a specific request execution should be elevated to high-fidelity capture.
- Sampling knob types: uniform, cohort-based, adaptive, and quorum-triggered.

Quorum signals (used in predicates)

1) SLO breach candidate: request latency > 95th percentile for route/model for the last 15 minutes.
2) Kernel anomaly: per-kernel execution time > kernel_baseline * 3 (fast local baseline).
3) Cross-tenant contention signal: GPU kernel preemption or eviction events observed within request lifetime.
4) KV cache warmup failure: expected cached prefix missing for an established session (session age > 1 minute).
5) Error family match: any 5xx or structured runtime error matching the incident regex list.

Quorum policy (default production)

- Elevate to high-fidelity capture when any two distinct quorum signals are true for the same request OR when a single critical signal is flagged (Error family match or GPU preemption).
- High-fidelity capture includes: complete kernel event stream, full per-token scheduler decisions, gpu telemetry slice, request input/output payloads (redacted), and KV cache deltas.

Sampling tiers and retention

- Baseline (always-on): lightweight request metrics and sparse trace IDs (1% uniform). Retention: 90 days aggregated metrics, 7 days indexed traces.
- Diagnostic (cohort-based): 5% of traffic per high-risk route (see table below) or cohort sampling determined by route annotations. Retention: 30 days indexed traces.
- Quorum-captured (elevated): retained for 90 days in compressed archive with access controls; access requires incident ticket and approval.

Operational table: sampling defaults by route profile

- low-latency-read: uniform 0.5% (embeddings, short completions).
- interactive-chat: uniform 1%, cohort 3% for power users.
- long-generation: uniform 2%, cohort 10% for pinned beta customers.
- batch-embedding-job: uniform 0.2%, cohort capture via job-id sampling 1%.

(Operators can override per-customer using route config in Redwood Console; see "How to override" below.)

Cost/benchmark impact guidance

- Turning on kernel-level event capture increases per-request telemetry payload by ~8–12KB and ingestion CPU by ~1.4x in our benchmarks. Expect storage 10x for full request-level captures vs. aggregated metrics.
- Benchmarks run with high-fidelity capture enabled should use the "telemetry-isolated" flag to prevent polluted baseline comparisons. See the CLI section below.

Implementation notes (runtime hooks)

- Kernel scheduler hooks: place a light-weight hook at kernel dispatch entry to emit a 64-byte token with request id and scheduling decision. Hooks must be non-blocking and batch-emitted at 50ms intervals.
- KV cache tracing: emit a compact diff (keys touched, miss/hit) with session id and hashed prefix. Do not include raw prompt text unless redaction pass is applied.
- Device handoff: emit handshake events with device ids, estimated queue depth, and kernel queue latency.

Sample quorum predicate (YAML)

quorum:
  version: 1
  rules:
    - id: slo_and_kernel
      description: "Latency spike + kernel abnormality"
      predicates:
        - signal: slo_breach_candidate
        - signal: kernel_anomaly
      require: 2
    - id: critical_error
      description: "Immediate capture on critical errors"
      predicates:
        - signal: error_family_match
      require: 1

How to override sampling in Console (step-by-step)

1) Navigate to Console > Runtime > Routes and select the route.
2) Click "Telemetry" tab.
3) Edit Sampling Profile: choose baseline/cohort/quorum-enabled.
4) Optional: attach a temporary experiment tag (telemetry.debug=true, expiry in 24h). Changes are audited and emitted as config diff to S3: s3://redwood-runtime-configs/telemetry-overrides.
5) Monitor cost impact: Console shows estimated daily ingestion delta before committing.

Runbook: incident capture and access flow (for SREs)

1) Triage: determine whether the incident is reproducible and whether quorum predicates would have captured examples.
2) If not captured, flip a cohort override for the affected route with a 10x cohort multiplier for 30 minutes. Use the CLI: redwood telemetry override --route <route> --multiplier 10 --duration 30m --reason "incident PID-<id>".
3) Collect captures: link to S3 tarball in the incident ticket. Retain copy in incident workspace (encrypted).
4) Postmortem: annotate the captured traces with kernel snapshot id, runtime version, and scheduler policy.

CLI examples

# Enable ephemeral high-fidelity capture for route
redwood telemetry override --route /v1/generate--chat --set quorum_enabled=true --duration 20m --owner sre-team

# Run benchmark without telemetry noise
redwood bench run --workload long-gen --telemetry-isolated=true --output ./bench-results

Privacy and redaction rules

- Request payloads are redacted by default: only prompt hashes and token counts are stored. Full text is captured only when: (a) customer consent is present, OR (b) explicit legal/incident approval is granted.
- PII redaction pipeline: apply token-level redaction that replaces probable PII tokens with <REDACTED_STRING> and emits confidence score.

Testing and rollout plan for changes to quorum policy

1) Developer preview: enable policy in the sandbox runtime (tag: telemetry-sandbox) for 1 week with 100% traffic in sandbox. Verify schema, CPU overhead <= +15%.
2) Canary: rollout 1% of production routes with telemetry-isolated benchmark. Monitor ingestion and per-token cost delta for 48h.
3) Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over rolling four-day windows. SRE gate: ingestion cost increase must be <= 30% of forecasted budget per stage.

Release notes (policy v1.2)

- 2026-01-18: v1.2 released. Key changes: added "cross-tenant contention" quorum signal, tightened default cohort rates for long-generation routes, introduced telemetry-isolated flag for benchmarks.

Known issues and mitigations

- #KT-1823: occasional race in kernel hook emission can drop the first scheduling token under high concurrency. Mitigation: bump batch flush window from 25ms to 50ms and retry on missing kernel snapshot.
- #KV-991: session-id collisions in high-throughput job batching caused misattribution in KV diffs. Mitigation: switch session-id generator to 128-bit random uuid and add job-id namespace.

Ownership and escalation

- Ownership: Observability Platform (owner) + Serving Runtime (maintainer). Primary contacts: observability@redwood.ai, runtime-oncall@redwood.ai.
- Escalation: if telemetry ingestion > 2x forecast, page Observability Platform lead and SRE. Use incident channel #telemetry-ops.

Appendix: schema snippets and sample JSON trace (compact)

- Compact trace example (fields explained):
{
  "trace_id": "abcd-1234",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "rw-open-7b",
  "events": ["kernel_dispatch:ts:...","kv_cache_delta:...","handoff:..."],
  "meta": "schema_v1"
}

- Telemetry cost estimator quick lookup (Console): per-100k requests estimated delta with kernel_capture=on: +$1,200/day (region=us-west-2, as of 2026-01).
